vo: Your AI agent says the work is done. ... Is it?
title: The manifesto

vo: In real repositories, agents drift. Rule files that share almost nothing. Seventeen checks nobody ran. Thirty-two hundred files, changed at once.
title: Agents drift

vo: Meet Majordomus. The supervisory layer for your AI agents.
title: Meet Majordomus

vo: When an agent says it's finished, Majordomus checks the scope, the state, and the tests. And when anything fails, it refuses.
title: Done is a contract

vo: And every proof leaves a record. The test, the commit, the tree, the time, and the exact command. Provenance, not promises.
title: Provenance, not promises
Written down is not enforced
vo: A rule is not enforced because it is written down. It is enforced when it is declared, validated, wired into a command, fails that command, is tested, blocks CI, and backs a claim. Anything less is documentation.

title: The repository checks itself
vo: And the repository checks itself. Majordomus doctor reads every rule, every projection and every hook, on every commit. Forty-four blocking rules, each with a validator. Zero failures.

title: Two hooks hold the line
vo: Two hooks hold the line. Every commit runs doctor. Every push runs the finish contract, and an unmet one stops the push. Until the first task starts, both stay quiet.

title: Numbers, measured or absent
vo: It will not sell you a number it never measured. Savings come only from recorded pairs of runs, with it and without it, on the same task, and both must pass. A run that saves tokens by failing is not a saving. And a number typed into prose is refused.

title: Uncertainty, reasoned on the record
vo: When a decision is uncertain, it is reasoned on the record. Evidence first. Advisors, if any are present, and their answers are evidence, never verdicts. The conclusion stays for the next session to read.
Install it with one line. Initialise your repository. Then start a task with a scope, and let your agents work.
title: Three commands
Work starts from intent
vo: Work starts from intent: what must become true, and the criteria that prove it. Intents become milestones, milestones become issues, and plan next names the one issue to take now.

title: Status, derived
vo: No issue stores its status. It is derived from what happened to it: started, verified, completed, and the evidence each step carries. Done is refused while a required proof is missing, and plan next recomputes the one issue to take.
Every session starts briefed. The task, its scope, the last handover's next action, who else is working, and what the release still owes. Nothing to rediscover.
title: Every session starts briefed

vo: Context is a tree. Each agent reads the documents from the root down to the path it works on. The nearest adds to its ancestors, and siblings never see each other. Nothing more, and nothing less.
title: Hierarchical context

vo: One policy writes every agent's instructions. Tasks live in the repository, not in a chat window.
title: Rules, written once

vo: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Zed, Antigravity, bb, or any client that speaks MCP. Each reads its own projection of the same policy.
title: Every client, one policy

vo: Models are declared data. Anthropic and OpenAI in the cloud, Ollama and LM Studio on your own machine. Routing picks one by need. Ask for local only, and it answers: nothing qualifies. Never a guess.
title: Models, declared

vo: Every operation is declared once. The command line, the HTTP API, the MCP tools, the OpenAPI document, the docs and the skills are generated from it, and a check fails the moment one drifts.
title: Declared once, projected everywhere
Versions, measured
vo: Versions are measured, not claimed. Every release compares the public surface with the last one. Something gone is a major, something new is a minor, and nothing changed owes nothing. The changelog writes itself.
One shared server per repository. The first client starts it, every next one attaches, and each sees the others. The same server answers over HTTP, with Swagger and the Cockpit.
title: One shared MCP server
The Cockpit
vo: And a person sees all of it in the Cockpit. The same server, the same registry, rendered for a person, with nothing of its own to drift.
Before they share a board, runtimes find each other. A signed beacon on the local network, a rendezvous hub further out. Every one is checked before it is heard, and none carries a secret.
title: Peer discovery

vo: Before work starts, every worker writes on the blackboard what it intends, and the paths it expects to touch. A claim, not a lock. Overlaps surface the moment they are written.
title: The blackboard

vo: Claude, Codex and Gemini share one board. When two reach for the same file, you hear about it before the merge.
title: One board, every agent
Checked before it is built
vo: The board says who is working now. Git says what was already built. Before a new module is written, every branch, local and remote, is asked what already claims its paths. And a decision number another branch already carries is refused at commit.

title: One claim, one winner
vo: When work must not overlap across machines, it is claimed exclusively. A second session is refused, and told which claim it meets. When two machines claim in the same heartbeat, every runtime names the same winner, never the last packet. A holder that stops beating loses its claim.

title: One branch, one worktree
vo: Parallel work needs parallel trees. Every branch has exactly one worktree, derived from git: the primary checkout keeps the trunk, every other branch lives beside it. A commit from the wrong place is refused.

title: Work moves through seats
vo: Work moves through seats. One seat lands green work in combined tops. One releases whenever master is ahead of the last tag. Repair lanes bring stale branches current, and each worker holds one issue. A seat is a claim, so it falls vacant when its holder stops beating.

title: Many pull requests, one run
vo: Pull requests land as a train. Each link is stacked on the one below, and every link's checks run at the same time. One run pays for several. A link merges only after the one it names, and git decides it is safe, never the stacking.
The mesh spans every machine you work on. The desktop at home. The rack in the datacenter, behind a TLS hub. The whole fleet across the company, on a private network.
title: Home, datacenter, company
Built once, reused everywhere
vo: Every build goes through the mesh cache. What one machine compiled, the next one reuses, and nobody sets a variable. When the store is down, the build stays local and says why. A script that goes around the cache is refused by a gate.
Every message is signed with the machine's own key. No one is trusted until you list them. A public address is reached over HTTPS only. And nothing a peer sends is ever executed.
title: Signed, listed, inert

vo: Sessions talk to each other through the mesh. One asks for a review, another answers it from a different machine. A handover published tonight is consumed tomorrow, wherever the work resumes.
title: Sessions talk to each other

vo: One stream follows every session, claim, handover and review on every linked machine, with the merges and the GitHub runs beside them. What names you comes first, and the noise is folded away.
title: One stream

vo: Close the laptop tonight. Tomorrow, any agent picks up the handover, exactly where the work stopped.
title: Work that outlives the chat

vo: And what a session learns outlives it too. Decisions become records: a hundred and sixty architecture decisions so far. Knowledge is derived at the end of every session, without a model, and a person promotes what deserves to stay.
title: What it learns stays learned
What is yours stays yours
vo: What is yours stays yours. Session state lives in the local half of the layer, which git ignores. Handovers, checkpoints and open sessions are written readable by their owner only, and none of them is ever committed.
Not your repository to change? Personal mode keeps the whole layer in your clone, and the team's tree stays byte for byte what they committed.
title: Personal mode

vo: It runs on your machine, never calls a model, and works with any agent.
title: Yours, entirely

vo: We believe done is a contract, not a feeling. That agents should prove, not promise. That the repository remembers what the chat forgets. ... AI agents were a leap forward. Trust is the next one.
title: The manifesto, No. 02

vo: Your agents say it's done. Majordomus makes them prove it. Majordomus dot dev.
title: Make them prove it

vo: Because tomorrow, again,
title: Again
